guards:
Hired soldiers in the Bastion's colours who walk the walls, keep the gate and turn out when trouble comes.

Each guard adds to the garrison's strength. Guards are paid every turn and eat from the stores; how many can be hired depends on the Garrison Hall. Hire and dismiss them on the Defense page.
mercenaries:
Hard-bitten fighters who turn up looking for work, usually after word of the Bastion gets around.

Mercenaries join through the Bastion's events and stay as extra defenders until they are dismissed or killed. They add to the garrison like guards.
facility-defenders:
The defenders the owners keep at their special facilities: a Barrack's soldiers, the guards posted at a workshop or a library.

They come from the dnd5e facilities on the owners' sheets and count toward the garrison, more so when the Armory is stocked. Assign them on the facilities themselves.
lieutenants:
Trusted officers who plan around the War Room's table.

Lieutenants are the hirelings of a War Room on an owner's sheet. They lead the Bastion's forces and come with the facility.
engine-crews:
The soldiers who wind, aim and load the ballistae on the walls.

Each Ballista Emplacement brings its own crew, and they add to the garrison's strength in a fight.
servants:
The cooks, maids, grooms and porters who keep the Bastion running from dawn to dark.

Servants are hired once there are Servants' Quarters for them, paid a little each turn, and they live and eat at the Bastion.
hirelings:
Skilled people who work the owners' facilities: a smith at the forge, a scribe in the library, a groom in the stables.

Hirelings come with the dnd5e facilities on the owners' sheets. They live at the Bastion and count toward its people.
building-crews:
Masons, carpenters and labourers who raise everything the Bastion builds.

A Bastion starts with one crew and can hire more, or house one in a Workers' Lodge. Each crew works on one project at a time, and extra crews on a project finish it sooner. Hired crews are paid every turn.
refugees:
Families fleeing war, famine or worse, who arrive at the gate with what they could carry.

Refugees who are taken in live at the Bastion and eat from its stores. A Guest Wing gives them somewhere to stay.
merchants:
Peddlers, caravans, merchant companies and the occasional exotic trader who stop at the Bastion to sell their wares.

How often they come and how rich their stock is depends on Accessibility, Prosperity, Renown and the Bastion's trade buildings. While a merchant is visiting, the owners can buy from the Trade page.
guests:
Visitors who stay a while: a renowned figure, someone seeking sanctuary, now and then a friendly monster or a sellsword.

Guests arrive through the Bastion's events. Some pay for their stay, some leave a letter of recommendation, and some help defend the walls.
visitors:
The steady traffic of a Bastion on a road: pilgrims, adventurers with a rumor, would-be recruits, the lord's tax collector, an envoy, now and then a spy.

A visitor may arrive each turn. Most bring news, coin or work; a few bring trouble. A Guest Wing makes paying visitors pay more.
caravans:
Wagons, drovers and a few hired swords on the road between the Bastion and another settlement.

A trade route starts as a request: a town or village asks, the owners accept, the party travels there to agree the terms, and the GM signs the contract once they have. From then on the caravans bring gold every turn, or food every day when the town sends grain or livestock, until the route is cancelled. A request nobody signs lapses. Caravans can be raided in dangerous country, and nothing gets through a siege.
